name: cp
description: Copies files and directories from one location to another.

flags.description: -R: copy directories recursively, including their contents.
Ask before overwriting an existing destination file.
Force copying by removing the destination file if it cannot be opened.
Print each file as it is copied.
Archive mode: same as -dR --preserve=all; ideal for backups.
Copy only when the source is newer than the destination or the destination is missing.

examples.explanation: Creates a copy of file.txt named backup.txt in the same directory.
Copies file.txt into the Documents directory, keeping its original name.
Copies the entire project directory, including all subdirectories, into backup/. The -r flag is required for directories.
Preserves the original file's permissions, owner, and timestamps in the copy.
Prompts before overwriting an existing destination file, protecting against accidental data loss.
Archive mode with verbose output — a reliable pattern for full directory backups.

about: cp copies file contents and, depending on options, metadata. Without -r it refuses to copy directories. Without -p or -a, the copy receives fresh timestamps and permissions derived from the umask, which frequently surprises users making backups.
Writing to a directory destination requires the directory to exist; cp does not create it for you.
useCases: Duplicate files or entire directory trees.
Back up configuration before editing: cp -a /etc/nginx /etc/nginx.bak.
Refresh copies only when sources changed with cp -u.
mistakes: Copying a directory without -r: cp dir/ other/ fails with "omitting directory".
Overwriting files unintentionally because -i was not used in scripts run as root.
warnings: cp overwrites existing destination files silently unless -i or -n is given. There is no built-in undo.
Do not use cp -r on /proc, /sys, or /dev — it can hang or produce errors; those are virtual filesystems.
distroNotes: cp is part of GNU coreutils on Linux. BSD cp supports -a and -p but lacks some GNU extensions such as --parents.
